text:
raj: Alert from nightly perf dash — sudden tail latency spike on dedicated pool A around 02:10. throughput steady but p95/p99 jumped ~3x. :eyes:

raj: attaching screenshot (nightly-panel) and `/metrics?range=last_6h` dump attached in thread.

infra-bot: [alert] nightdash: latency_spike detected for pool=dedicated-A, metric=p99_latency, threshold=250ms, observed=820ms, time=2026-03-18T02:11:03Z

tyler: saw this too. started ~02:05, aligns with the big merge that landed last night (PR #3456 — kernel-routing refactor).

amanda: can someone confirm if KV eviction rate changed? that usually explains tail spikes.

lucy: quick grep from metrics node1: ```
kv_evictions{pool="dedicated-A"}  =  0.0
kv_prefetch_hits{pool="dedicated-A"} = 0.12
kernel_selector_fallbacks_total{pool="dedicated-A"} = 452
kernel_selector_choice_latency_ms{pool="dedicated-A"} = 14.7
```

lucy: prefetch hits down, selector fallbacks up — smells like selector started choosing non-optimal kernels or hitting a runtime path that disables KV hints.

sre-oncall: can we bisect to the merge? tag @tyler @amanda — if PR3456 changed selector ordering, we should try reverting it on canary or replaying CI. This is blocking the morning rollout.

tyler: starting bisection locally: will roll back incremental commits from PR3456 in staging to reproduce. grabbing the nightly trace.

devex: FYI CI shows perf regression on the merge job: `ci-perf/e2e/selector` failed with p99 > baseline. Logs: ```
[2026-03-18T01:58:12Z] warm-start: kernel A ok
[2026-03-18T02:04:01Z] kernel-selector: fallback to generic-kernel, reason=cost_model_mismatch
[2026-03-18T02:04:02Z] kv-cache: hint-miss for prefix uid=0x9f3a
[2026-03-18T02:04:02Z] batching: window_shrink trigger=selector-latency
```

amanda: if CI already failed, we should block rollout. I'll flip the rollout flag for the candidate build in the console.

raj: flipping to hold now. :no_entry: Can we get a minimal repro script to exercise hot-path (short sequences, many concurrent requests) so we can test a quick patch?

tyler: creating repro: `stress-run --pool dedicated-A --seq-len 64 --concurrency 80 --prometheus-prefix nightly_repro` — running against staging. will post results in 10m.

lucy: profiler around 02:06 shows CPU time spent in `select_kernel_by_cost()` increased x4 and lots of small kernel launches. KV cache lookups also show `false` for `hint_valid`. suspect change in ordering removed the early-path that validates hints.

amanda: propose temporary revert of the ordering change from PR3456 to restore old selector heuristic while we debug. Agree? @raj @sre-oncall

sre-oncall: +1 — revert on canary first, then prod if stable. prioritize a safety revert today.

tyler: I can prep the revert PR and a canary rollout. will attach perf baseline comparison after canary warms up.

raj: thanks. once revert is up, please also run the repro and CI perf job to confirm p99 back to normal. add a short note in the release channel so product doesn't try to promote.

devex: adding a checklist: 1) block rollout (done), 2) create revert PR (tyler), 3) run repro + CI perf (tyler/devex), 4) confirm p99/resolved (lucy/sre-oncall), 5) follow-up root cause ticket (eng-runtime-1234).

tyler: revert PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3470 — starting canary deploy.

infra-bot: [deploy] canary deployed runtime@3470-revert to pool=canary-1 at 2026-03-18T03:05:12Z

tyler: canary metrics show p99 back to baseline within 15m of warmup. staging CI perf also green. going to promote after +30m observation.

raj: excellent. please keep notes in the incident ticket and mark the merge as blocked until we finish a root cause fix and test.

amanda: filed follow-up: ENGRT-1234 "kernel-selector ordering introduced KV hint invalidation" with repro and profiler outputs.

lucy: leaving a tiny profiler snippet we used: ```
perf record -e cycles -a -- sleep 30
perf report --no-children | head -n 40
# grep shows select_kernel_by_cost high at 42% CPU
```

raj: nice work everyone. postmortem/action items after root cause. :thumbsup:
